issues.description: Extract a named predicate like `isLayerStatement(node)` instead of the inline negated conjunction.
issues.detail: `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` buries the CSS-spec invariant (statement-form @layer allowed before @import; block-form not) inside a dense five-clause boolean. A named helper or inverted positive form would make the intent self-evident at the call site and survive future maintenance.

issues.description: Replace `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` with a direct shape check (`node.nodes == null` or equivalent).
issues.detail: PostCSS represents block-less at-rules by the absence of `nodes`; `typeof === 'undefined'` is defensive verbiage that conflates AST shape with a JS idiom and leaks an implementation detail. A direct null check or typed helper matches surrounding code style and states the precondition on the AST shape itself.

issues.description: Add the symmetric accept-case test: `@layer foo;` (statement form) before `@import` must remain valid.
issues.detail: The diff adds the reject case for `@layer foo {}` before `@import` but does not pin the complementary accept case for the statement form. Without it, a future refactor could flip the predicate and silently regress the originally allowed behavior. One additional fixture locks the distinction in both directions.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously judges the fix correct and minimal: it restores the CSS Cascade distinction between statement-form `@layer foo;` (allowed before `@import`) and block-form `@layer foo {}` (not allowed). All six reviewers converge on the same three polish items, all P2: the predicate is expressed as a negated conjunction that obscures intent, `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` is a brittle proxy for AST shape, and the test suite asserts only the reject case without pinning the symmetric accept case. Verdict: ACCEPT after trivial cleanup; nothing rises to a blocker.
